Exercise A

Lesen & Erkennen

Lies den Text und wähle für jede Lücke die passende Form.

Bevor du liest

Diese Frage wird nicht bewertet — schreib einfach, was dir einfällt.

Ein Morgen in Leons Leben

So funktioniert es: Gewohnheiten und Fakten → Simple Present („He goes to school by bus“). Was gerade passiert → is/are + -ing („He is waiting for the bus now“).

1 Leon up at seven o’clock.

2 Right now, he on the bus to school.

3 He to a comprehensive school in Berlin.

4 At the moment, he for a maths test with his friend Ben.

5 His best friend next door to him.

6 Look! The teacher into the classroom.

Exercise B

Simple oder Progressive?

Acht Sätze — lies die Signalwörter, sie verraten die Form.

Task

1 Water at 100 degrees Celsius.

2 Listen! Somebody in the music room.

3 My sister meat — she’s a vegetarian.

4 We dinner right now — can I call you back?

5 The train to Hamburg at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

6 I a really good book this week.

7 He football every Saturday with his team.

8 What this weekend?

Exercise C

Statische Verben

know, like, want, understand — diese Verben stehen fast nie im Progressive.

Task

1 I the question now — thanks for explaining!

2 This soup great — can I have the recipe?

3 Be quiet, please! She about a difficult problem.

4 the answer, or shall I tell you?

5 We usually walk to school, but today we the bus.

6 Look at this photo — the man next to me?

Exercise D

Schreiben

Beschreib deinen typischen Schultag — und was diese Woche anders ist.

Task

Schreib 6–8 Sätze: Was machst du normalerweise (Simple Present mit usually, every day), und was passiert gerade in dieser Woche Besonderes (Present Progressive mit this week, at the moment)?
